title: Signature Joint Embedding Search — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Multimodal search represents every item — a paragraph, an image, an audio clip — as a vector in one shared embedding space, so similarity becomes a distance computation regardless of original format. At query time the query is embedded the same way and the nearest vectors are returned, which lets a text query find a diagram that no keyword could reach. Cosine similarity is the workhorse metric because it compares direction rather than magnitude. Real systems train these joint spaces on paired data; the geometry here demonstrates the retrieval math on synthetic vectors. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
provenance: JAH Databases archive-intelligence tools program, lane T2a — Signature original authored for Justin Addam Higgins.

title: Signature Modality Adapters — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Before anything can share an embedding space, each modality needs an adapter that turns its raw form into features: token counts for text, color histograms for images, spectral summaries for audio. Adapters are small, replaceable functions with a uniform interface — bytes in, feature vector out — so new formats plug in without touching the search core. Each adapter also reports a confidence, because a truncated audio file deserves less trust than a clean one. This adapter layer is what makes 'multimodal' an engineering reality instead of a slogan. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature Cross-Modal Retrieval — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. The most striking multimodal trick is cross-modal retrieval: a text query returning images, or a hummed tune returning recordings, with no shared keywords at all. It works because the joint embedding space was trained to place matching pairs near each other — the caption 'red bridge' lands beside photos of red bridges. At retrieval time the query is embedded by its own modality encoder and matched against everything else in the space. Evaluation uses recall at k on held-out pairs, which directly measures whether the cross-modal mapping generalizes. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature Late Score Fusion — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. When each modality runs its own specialized search, late fusion combines the per-modality score lists into one ranking. Scores are first normalized — z-scores or min-max — because a text engine's 0.9 and an image engine's 0.9 mean different things, then a weighted sum merges them with weights tuned on validation queries. Items found by several modalities get a consistency bonus, which rewards agreement across independent evidence. Late fusion is simple, robust, and the default ensemble method in production multimodal systems. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature Perceptual Hashing — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Perceptual hashes fingerprint media so that near-identical items — a resized image, a re-encoded clip — hash to nearby values, unlike cryptographic hashes where one pixel flips everything. A simple average hash shrinks the image to 8x8 grayscale, then sets each bit by whether the pixel beats the mean, yielding a 64-bit fingerprint. Hamming distance between fingerprints measures visual similarity, and databases index these hashes for fast near-duplicate lookup. This is how archives find copies and derivatives without comparing raw bytes. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
